data.Name: William Pitt
data.Bio: The Elder, Secretary of State who shaped the British war effort in the colonies.

data.Name: George Anson
data.Bio: First Lord of the Admiralty, circumnavigator of the globe, naval reformer.

data.Name: Henry Pelham
data.Bio: Prime Minister of Great Britain, architect of colonial taxation policy.

data.Name: Robert Clive
data.Bio: Clive of India, founder of the British Indian empire, advisor on colonial affairs.

data.Name: James Wolfe
data.Bio: Major-General who scaled the cliffs of Quebec to win New France for Britain.

data.Name: Jeffery Amherst
data.Bio: Commander-in-Chief of British forces in North America, conqueror of New France.

data.Name: Diego de Peza y Valle
data.Bio: Captain-General of Cuba and the Floridas under the Bourbon crown; commander of San Marcos de Apalache and the Havana garrison.

data.Name: Alonso Fernandez de Heredia
data.Bio: Lieutenant-General of the Captaincy General of Cuba and the Floridas; inspector of the coastal presidios.

data.Name: Pedro de Horruytiner
data.Bio: Intendant of the Captaincy General of Cuba; auditor of war and finance of the Floridas frontier garrisons.

data.Name: Julian de Arriaga y Rivera
data.Bio: Secretary of State for the Marine at Madrid; directed the colonial administration of the Floridas and Cuba.

data.Name: Jose Carlos de Aguila
data.Bio: Auditor de Guerra and brigadier of the Floridas frontier; commanded the Apalache and Pensacola presidios.

data.Name: Manuel de Cagigal de la Vega
data.Bio: Marquis de Cagigal y la Vega, veteran of the Spanish fleet at Cartagena; Captain-General of Cuba and the Floridas.

data.Name: Louis-Joseph de Montcalm
data.Bio: Marquis de Montcalm, commander of French forces in New France; defender of Quebec against the British in 1759.

data.Name: Pierre Francois de Rigaud
data.Bio: Marquis de Vaudreuil-Cavagnial, Governor-General of New France 1755-1760; negotiated with the western Indigenous nations.

data.Name: Antoine-Louis Rouille
data.Bio: Count of Jouy, Minister of the Marine 1749-1754; directed French colonial policy from Versailles.

data.Name: Jean-Baptiste de la Rochefoucauld
data.Bio: Duke de la Rochefoucauld, French colonial secretary; envoy between the court of Versailles and the colonies.

data.Name: Pierre de Bougainville
data.Bio: Aide-de-camp to Montcalm in New France; later the first French circumnavigator of the globe.

data.Name: Francois-Gaston de Levis
data.Bio: Brigadier of the French armies in New France; succeeded Montcalm and led the 1760 counter-offensive against the British.
Viceroy of New Spain under Ferdinand VI; defended the Caribbean ports against British raids; knight of the Order of the Golden Fleece.
data.Name: Juan Francisco de Revillagigedo

data.Bio: Field Marshal of New Spain; veteran of the Italian campaigns; reorganized the colonial army of Mexico City.
data.Name: José de Amezquita

data.Bio: Captain-General of the Captaincy General of Guatemala; veteran of the Bourbon army; knight of the Order of Santiago.
data.Name: Matías de Aréizaga

data.Bio: Minister of the Indies under Ferdinand VI; directed the colonial administration of the Viceroyalty of New Spain.
data.Name: Marqués de la Ensenada

data.Bio: Engineer of the New Spanish fortifications; designed the masonry bastions of San Juan de Ulúa.
data.Name: Francisco de Aguirre

data.Bio: Brigadier of the Caribbean fleet; commanded the guarda costa of New Spain; knight of the Order of San Fernando.
data.Name: Manuel de Cagigal de la Vega
Kiasola
data.Bio: Cherokee chief allied with the Iroquois Confederacy during the 1750s; maintained peace across the Ohio frontier.

data.Name: Hendrick Theyanoguin
data.Bio: Mohawk sachem of the Iroquois, ally of the British in King George's War, killed at the Battle of Lake George in 1755.

data.Name: Joseph Brant
data.Bio: Mohawk war chief of the Iroquois Confederacy; led pan-Indigenous resistance during the American Revolution.

data.Name: Skenandoah
data.Bio: Oneida chief of the Iroquois, friend of the colonial settlers, advocate for peace and diplomacy.

data.Name: Karonghyontye
data.Bio: Sachem of the Mohawk, speaker for the Iroquois council at Onondaga, keeper of the wampum belts.

data.Name: George Croghan
data.Bio: Deputy superintendent of Indian Affairs for the British colonies; longtime intermediary with the western nations.

data.Name: Atakullakulla
data.Bio: Cherokee chief, peace advocate during the Anglo-Cherokee War; long-time friend of the British colonies.

data.Name: Oconostota
data.Bio: Cherokee chief of the Overhill towns; military leader at the siege of Fort Loudoun.

data.Name: Dragging Canoe
data.Bio: Cherokee war chief; led resistance against American frontier expansion after the Cherokee-American wars.

data.Name: Corn Tassel
data.Bio: Cherokee chief of the Overhill; maintained peace treaties with the southern colonies.

data.Name: Old Tassel
data.Bio: Cherokee chief of the Cherokee council; signer of treaties with the new United States.

data.Name: Chief Doublehead
data.Bio: Cherokee chief of the Chickamauga faction; raider of the Cumberland settlements.

data.Name: Comcomly
data.Bio: Chinook chief on the Columbia River, keeper of trade at Baker Bay; ally of the maritime fur trade.

data.Name: Coboway
data.Bio: Chinook chief of the lower Columbia; signed treaties with Pacific maritime traders.

data.Name: Concomly the Younger
data.Bio: Chinook chief, son of Comcomly; maintained Chinook neutrality in maritime conflicts.

data.Name: Tahlahorten
data.Bio: Shoshone chief of the Lemhi band, ally of the Columbia drainage traders; Salmon River leader.

data.Name: Chief Washakie
data.Bio: Shoshone chief of the eastern band; led peace councils along the Snake River.

data.Name: Old Toweeto
data.Bio: Chinook-Tillamook chief; mediator of the lower Columbia treaties.

data.Name: Viceroy Teodoro de Croix
data.Bio: First Viceroy of Peru under the Bourbon reforms; modernizer of colonial administration in Lima.

data.Name: Aurelio Malavia
data.Bio: Captain-General of the Viceroyalty of Peru; commanded the loyalist militias in the south.

data.Name: Manuel de Amat y Junyent
data.Bio: Viceroy of Peru from 1761 to 1776; reorganized colonial defenses of the Pacific coast.

data.Name: Jose de Armendariz
data.Bio: Viceroy of Peru, reorganized tax collection; bridged the audiencia and the corregidores.

data.Name: Sebastian de Eslava
data.Bio: Viceroy of New Granada, also captain-general of the southern Pacific seaboard; reorganized Cartagena and Quito.

data.Name: Pedro de Cevallos
data.Bio: Veteran soldier and Viceroy of the Rio de la Plata, also active in Peruvian administration; defender of the southern Pacific.

data.Name: Marques de Pombal
data.Bio: Chief Minister of Portugal, reformer of the colonial economy after the Lisbon earthquake; architect of the Luso-Brazilian bureaucracy.

data.Name: Conde de Lippe
data.Bio: Wilhelm of Schaumburg-Lippe, reformer of the Portuguese army in Brazil after the Spanish frontier wars.

data.Name: Joao da Silva
data.Bio: Portuguese ambassador to Vienna; architect of Luso-Brazilian colonial policy, reformer of the Bahian captaincy.

data.Name: Conde de Bobadela
data.Bio: Governor of Rio de Janeiro and the southern captaincies; founder of new colonial towns along the Atlantic coast.

data.Name: Andre de Mello
data.Bio: Portuguese colonial administrator in the Amazon basin; explorer of the great rivers of the Maranhao captaincy.

data.Name: Rodrigo de Souza
data.Bio: Portuguese noble defending the southern borders of Brazil against Spanish incursions from the Rio de la Plata.

data.Name: Lautaro
data.Bio: Mapuche toqui who led resistance against the Spanish in the Arauco War; trained in the Spanish camps before his uprising.

data.Name: Caupolican
data.Bio: Mapuche toqui of the confederation; chosen leader of the southern peoples during the early Arauco War.

data.Name: Colo Colo
data.Bio: Mapuche toqui and counselor; principal speaker of the confederated toqui council.

data.Name: Pelantaro
data.Bio: Mapuche toqui; led the uprising that captured and killed Governor Martin Garcia Onez de Loyola.

data.Name: Anganamon
data.Bio: Toqui of the confederated peoples; led the parliaments of the Bio Bio frontier.

data.Name: Curillan
data.Bio: Mapuche chief of the Araucania; ally of the frontier parliaments with the Spanish.

data.Name: Toqui Huyeman
data.Bio: Guaycuruan chief of the Gran Chaco; leader of the western mocovi alliance.

data.Name: Quimili
data.Bio: Toba (Qom) chief of the Chaco central; principal speaker of the northern mocovi league.

data.Name: Caingua
data.Bio: Guarani chief of the southern Chaco; keeper of the eastern yvy maraey frontier.

data.Name: Tabare
data.Bio: Charrua chief of the eastern pampas; leader of the Montevideo frontier.

data.Name: Lambare
data.Bio: Payagua chief of the Paraguay river; principal orator of the Gran Chaco confederation.

data.Name: Yrupe
data.Bio: Abipon chief of the Pilcomayo; allied cacique of the northern Chaco.

data.Name: Pedro de Bourbon
data.Bio: Brother of the vicereine, Bourbon prince in charge of the colonial secretariat.

data.Name: Blas de Lezo
data.Bio: One-eyed, one-legged, one-handed admiral of Cartagena, scourge of the British navy.

data.Name: Pedro de Cevallos
data.Bio: Veteran soldier and colonial governor of the Rio de la Plata, defender of the southern frontiers.

data.Name: Rafael de Eslava
data.Bio: Captain-General of Caracas, defender of the Venezuelan coast.

data.Name: Jose de Solis y Folch de Cardona
data.Bio: Spanish Brigadier and inspector of the Atlantic fleet; Captain-General of the Cartagena de Indias fortress.

data.Name: Juan de Manzanet y Pinillos
data.Bio: Oidor of the Audiencia of Santa Fe; treasurer of the Viceroyalty of New Granada and administrator of the Cartagena customs.
